subject: Hospitality
title: Metasearch: The Aggregator Layer
description: A micro-lesson that makes Metasearch: The Aggregator Layer usable.

hook.text: Trivago, Kayak, and Google Hotels don't sell rooms—they compare prices across OTAs and hotel sites. They search the searchers.

buildup.text: Metasearch sets up the core claim, the assumptions, and the stakes.

discovery.text: Hotels can advertise on metasearch to drive direct bookings, bypassing OTAs when guests click through to the hotel's own website.

twist.text: Metasearch added yet another fee layer. Hotels now pay OTAs, metasearch platforms, and search engines—all for the same guest.

climax.text: The distribution ecosystem has become a maze. Revenue managers must optimize across dozens of channels simultaneously.

punchline.text: A search engine for search engines. Distribution keeps getting more complex.

quiz.question: What do metasearch sites like Trivago do?
options: They compare prices across OTAs and hotel websites side by side
